name: József Csatári
milestone_by_age_26: Won bronze at the 1966 European Wrestling Championships in freestyle wrestling at 97 kg, and later Olympic bronze at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics at age 24.
early_history_summary: Csatári tried multiple sports as a youth in Budapest before finding wrestling at around age 15 at Kinizsi Húsos, while working as a butcher at a slaughterhouse. He debuted with the Hungarian adult national team in 1963 at age 19 and was coached by Olympic champion Károly Kárpáti at Bp. Honvéd.
primary_leverage_engine: Physical talent and elite training environment
family_context_summary: Working-class background in Budapest; worked as a butcher at a slaughterhouse before finding wrestling through a coworker.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Hungarian national wrestling system, Olympic champion coach, Olympic champion training partner, Budapest wrestling ecosystem
evidence_summary: Csatári grew up in Budapest in a working-class family, working as a butcher before discovering wrestling through a coworker at the slaughterhouse. He joined Kinizsi Húsos and quickly rose through the Hungarian wrestling system, training with two-time Olympic champion István Kozma and later being coached by Olympic champion Károly Kárpáti at Bp. Honvéd. The Hungarian national wrestling program was one of the world's strongest, providing elite coaching, training partners, and competition opportunities that accelerated his development.
starting_point: Born in Budapest to a working-class family; became a butcher and worked at the slaughterhouse before discovering wrestling through a coworker.
current_position: Died on January 30, 2021, at age 77 in Budapest; final role: retired wrestler who worked at the Honvéd Clubhouse and later returned to the slaughterhouse before retiring in 1985.

trajectory.event: Debuted with the Hungarian adult national wrestling team, finishing 6th at the World Championships in Greco-Roman wrestling at 97 kg.
Won bronze at the European Wrestling Championships in freestyle wrestling at 97 kg.
Won Olympic bronze medal in freestyle wrestling at 97 kg at the Mexico City Olympics.
Won silver medal at the World Wrestling Championships in Greco-Roman wrestling.
Won second Olympic bronze medal in freestyle wrestling at 100 kg at the Munich Olympics.
Retired from competitive wrestling with 19 individual and 21 team national championships.
Died on January 30, 2021, in Budapest after a long illness.

name: Bert Sakmann
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; was still a medical student at the Universities of Tübingen and Munich. His Nobel Prize-winning patch-clamp technique was developed in the 1970s-1980s, with the Nobel Prize awarded in 1991 at age 49.
early_history_summary: Sakmann studied medicine at the Universities of Tübingen and Munich, becoming interested in neurophysiology during his studies. He became a research assistant at the Max Planck Institute for Psychiatry in 1969-1970, after age 26.
evidence_summary: Sakmann was still a medical student at age 26, with no independently verifiable milestone by that age. His groundbreaking patch-clamp technique work with Erwin Neher began in the 1970s at the Max Planck Institute, and the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded in 1991 when he was 49.

name: George Kerr
milestone_by_age_26: Won gold in the 400m and 4x400m relay at the 1959 Pan American Games and back-to-back NCAA Championships in 1959 and 1960, followed by Olympic bronze in the 800m and 4x400m relay at the 1960 Rome Olympics at age 22.
early_history_summary: Kerr grew up in rural Hanover Parish, Jamaica, and was discovered as a running talent when PE teacher Ben Francis saw him chase a bus for a mile. He attended Knockalva Agricultural School and earned a scholarship to the University of Illinois, where he won seven Big Ten titles and two NCAA championships.
primary_leverage_engine: Physical talent and collegiate athletic pipeline
family_context_summary: From rural Hanover Parish, Jamaica; attended Knockalva Agricultural School before earning a scholarship to the University of Illinois.
primary_early_advantage_tags: University of Illinois scholarship, NCAA track program, PE teacher discovery, rural Jamaica upbringing
evidence_summary: Kerr was discovered as a running talent in rural Jamaica when PE teacher Ben Francis saw him chase a bus for a mile, leading to enrollment at Knockalva Agricultural School and eventually a scholarship to the University of Illinois. The US collegiate athletics system provided elite coaching, facilities, and competition that propelled him to NCAA titles and Pan American Games gold by age 21, and Olympic bronze by 22. His rural Jamaican upbringing with limited resources made the scholarship pathway critical to his development.
starting_point: Born in Hanover Parish, Jamaica, to a rural family; discovered as a running talent when a PE teacher saw him chase a bus for a mile, leading to enrollment at Knockalva Agricultural School.
current_position: Died on June 15, 2012, at age 74 in Kingston, Jamaica; final role: retired athlete regarded as a Jamaican Olympic trailblazer.

trajectory.event: Won gold in 400m and 4x400m relay at the Pan American Games in Chicago and the NCAA championship in 880 yards.
Won Olympic bronze medals in the 800m and 4x400m relay at the Rome Olympics competing for the British West Indies.
Won the British AAA Championships title in the 880 yards event.
Won double gold (440 yards and 4x440 relay) and silver (880 yards) at the Commonwealth Games; named Jamaican Sportsman of the Year.
Finished fourth in the 800m and 4x400m relay at the Tokyo Olympics, breaking the Olympic record for 800m in the semifinals.
Won bronze in the 880 yards at the Commonwealth Games in Kingston, Jamaica.
Died on June 15, 2012, in Kingston, Jamaica, after complications from heart surgery.

name: Joan Harrison
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold in the 100m backstroke at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics at age 16, becoming the first South African swimmer to win Olympic gold.
early_history_summary: Harrison grew up in East London, South Africa, with a swimming mother and rugby-playing father. By age 13 she held multiple national records and won national championships, and at 14 she won gold in the 440 yards freestyle at the 1950 British Empire Games, breaking the Games record by 13 seconds.
primary_leverage_engine: Physical talent and sporting family heritage
family_context_summary: Born in East London, South Africa, to a sporting family; her mother was a swimmer and her father played rugby.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a swimmer, providing early exposure to the sport; father played rugby, creating a sporting household environment.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Sporting family heritage, swimming mother, national records at 13, Olympic gold at 16, early swimming immersion
evidence_summary: Harrison was born into a sporting family in East London, South Africa, with a swimming mother and rugby-playing father who provided early immersion in sport. She was a prodigy, holding national records and winning senior national championships at age 13, and winning gold at the British Empire Games at 14. Her Olympic gold at 16 made her the first South African swimmer to achieve that feat, a record unmatched for 44 years.
starting_point: Born in East London, South Africa, to a sporting family; her mother was a swimmer and her father played rugby, providing early immersion in sport.
current_position: Died on May 20, 2025, at age 89; final role: retired swimmer who became the first South African to win Olympic swimming gold and later pursued field hockey.

trajectory.event: Won gold in the 440 yards freestyle at the British Empire Games in Auckland, breaking the Games record by 13 seconds and declared outstanding woman swimmer of the Games.
Won Olympic gold in the 100m backstroke at the Helsinki Olympics, becoming the first South African swimmer to win Olympic gold.
Won two gold, one silver, and one bronze at the British Empire and Commonwealth Games in Vancouver.
Retired from international competitive swimming, though she won national championships in backstroke and individual medley that year.
Died on May 20, 2025.

name: Janne Ahonen
milestone_by_age_26: Won individual gold in the normal hill at the 1997 World Championships at age 19, and team gold at the 1995 World Championships at age 17; also won the Four Hills Tournament in 1998/99 at age 21.
early_history_summary: Ahonen was born in Lahti, Finland, one of the world's ski jumping capitals, and joined the local club Lahden Hiihtoseura. He won the junior world championship at age 15 in 1993 and made his World Cup debut in December 1992 at age 15, competing at the senior World Championships that same year.
primary_leverage_engine: Early specialization and frontier geography immersion
family_context_summary: Born in Lahti, Finland, a major ski jumping center; joined the local club Lahden Hiihtoseura as a youth.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Lahti ski jumping capital, Lahden Hiihtoseura club, Finnish national team, world-class facilities from childhood, junior world champion at 15
evidence_summary: Ahonen was born in Lahti, Finland, one of the world's premier ski jumping cities, and joined the local club Lahden Hiihtoseura, giving him access to world-class facilities and coaching from childhood. He was a prodigy, winning the junior world championship at 15 and making his World Cup debut the same year. The combination of frontier geography immersion in Lahti and the Finnish national ski jumping pipeline accelerated his development to World Championship gold by age 19.
starting_point: Born in Lahti, Finland, a world-renowned ski jumping city; joined the local club Lahden Hiihtoseura as a youth, giving him access to world-class ski jumping facilities from childhood.
current_position: Retired from competitive ski jumping in 2018 after a 26-year career; also competed in drag racing; resides in Hollola, Finland.

trajectory.event: Won the junior world championship and competed at the senior World Championships in Falun, making his World Cup debut in December 1992.
Won team gold at the World Championships in Thunder Bay in the team large hill event.
Won individual gold in the normal hill at the World Championships in Trondheim, plus another team gold.
Won the Four Hills Tournament for the first time, the first of a record five career victories in the event.
Won the World Cup overall title for the 2003/04 season, the first of two consecutive overall titles.
Won second consecutive World Cup overall title and individual gold in the large hill at the World Championships; named Finnish Sports Personality of the Year.
Retired from competitive ski jumping after his final World Cup appearance in Lahti, ending a 26-year competitive career.

name: Manny Pacquiao
milestone_by_age_26: Won the WBC flyweight world title on December 4, 1998, at age 19, by knocking out Chatchai Sasakul in the eighth round, becoming a world champion.
early_history_summary: Pacquiao grew up in extreme poverty in Kibawe, Bukidnon, Philippines, quit school at 10, and left home at 14 to pursue boxing in Manila, living on the streets. He started boxing at 12, was considered the best junior boxer in the southern Philippines by 15, and made his professional debut at 16 in January 1995.
family_context_summary: Born into extreme poverty in Kibawe, Bukidnon, Philippines; raised by a single mother with six siblings; quit school at age 10 and left home at 14.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented; an uncle began training him in boxing at age 12. His brother Bobby also became a professional boxer.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Extreme poverty, street fights for money, professional debut at 16, Philippine boxing culture, national amateur team, uncle as first trainer
evidence_summary: Pacquiao was born into extreme poverty in the Philippines, raised by a single mother with six siblings, and quit school at 10. He started boxing at 12, was fighting in street bouts for money, and left home at 14 to pursue boxing in Manila, living on the streets before joining the Philippine national amateur team. His adversity created urgency and a distinctive fighting style, and the Philippine boxing culture provided a pathway from street fights to professional debut at 16 and a world title at 19.
starting_point: Born into extreme poverty in Kibawe, Bukidnon, Philippines; raised in a shack by a single mother with six siblings, quit school at 10, and left home at 14 to pursue boxing in Manila.
current_position: Former professional boxer and politician; served as Senator of the Philippines (2016-2022); net worth estimated at approximately $220 million; resides in the Philippines.

trajectory.event: Made professional boxing debut on January 22, winning by unanimous decision against Edmund Ignacio.
Won his first major world title, the WBC flyweight championship, by knocking out Chatchai Sasakul on December 4.
Won the IBF super bantamweight title by defeating Lehlo Ledwaba, beginning his rise through multiple weight divisions.
Defeated Oscar De La Hoya, establishing himself as a global boxing superstar.
Fought Floyd Mayweather Jr. in the highest-grossing boxing match in history.
Elected as Senator of the Philippines, serving until 2022.
Became the oldest welterweight world champion by winning the WBA welterweight title, a Guinness World Record.

name: Tomas Svensson
milestone_by_age_26: Won World Championship gold with Sweden at the 1990 IHF Men's World Championship in Czechoslovakia at age 22, and European Championship gold in 1994 at age 26.
early_history_summary: Svensson grew up in Eskilstuna, Sweden, and naturally joined the local handball club GUIF, making his senior debut in the Swedish top division at age 15. He earned his first national team cap in 1988 at age 20 and was a key force in Sweden's 1990 World Championship victory.
primary_leverage_engine: Early specialization and elite national team pipeline
family_context_summary: Born and raised in Eskilstuna, Sweden; naturally joined the local handball club GUIF.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Swedish national handball team, local club GUIF, senior debut at 15, Swedish handball golden era, Eskilstuna handball culture
evidence_summary: Svensson grew up in Eskilstuna, Sweden, where he naturally joined the local handball club GUIF and made his senior debut in the Swedish top division at age 15. The Swedish national handball program was one of the world's best, and he earned his first cap at 20 before winning World Championship gold at 22. His early immersion in a strong handball town and access to the elite Swedish national team pipeline were critical to his rapid development.
starting_point: Born and raised in Eskilstuna, Sweden; joined the local handball club GUIF and made his senior debut in the Swedish top division at age 15.
current_position: Retired from professional handball in 2012; currently serves as goalkeeping coach for FC Barcelona and the Swedish men's national handball team.

trajectory.event: Made his first cap for the Swedish national handball team.
Won World Championship gold with Sweden in Czechoslovakia, a breakthrough that led to a contract with Atlético Madrid.
Won European Championship gold with Sweden in Portugal.
Won his first EHF Champions League title with CD Bidasoa, starting a run of six consecutive Champions League titles.
Won second World Championship gold and third European Championship gold with Sweden.
Retired from professional handball after a season with Rhein-Neckar Löwen, ending a 24-year career with 327 national team caps.

name: Jean Van Hamme
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; was studying business administration and working as a journalist and in marketing at Philips. First comic script (Epoxy) published in 1968 at age 29; breakthrough with Thorgal in 1977 at age 38.
early_history_summary: Van Hamme studied business administration at the Solvay Brussels School and worked as a journalist and in the marketing department of Philips before becoming a full-time writer in 1976.
family_context_summary: Born in Brussels, Belgium; studied business administration at the Solvay Brussels School of Economics and Management.
evidence_summary: Van Hamme was still a student and corporate professional at age 26, with no independently verifiable creative milestone by that age. His first comic script was published at 29, and his major breakthrough with Thorgal came at 38, making him one of Europe's most prominent comic writers.

name: Daniel Castellani
milestone_by_age_26: Won bronze at the 1982 FIVB World Championship with Argentina as captain at age 21, and bronze at the 1983 Pan American Games at age 22.
early_history_summary: Castellani was born in La Lucila, Buenos Aires Province, and joined the Argentine national volleyball team in 1976 at age 15. He was a key leader of Argentina's celebrated 'Generation of '82' that won World Championship bronze on home soil.
primary_leverage_engine: Physical talent and national team pipeline
family_context_summary: Born in La Lucila, Buenos Aires Province, Argentina; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Argentine national volleyball team, Generation of '82, captain role, 195 cm height, early national team debut at 15
evidence_summary: Castellani joined the Argentine national volleyball team at age 15 in 1976, benefiting from the country's developing volleyball program. As captain of Argentina's 'Generation of '82,' he led the team to a World Championship bronze on home soil at 21 and an Olympic bronze at 27. His early entry into the national team pipeline and physical stature (195 cm) were key factors in his rapid development, though family background is not documented.
starting_point: Born in La Lucila, Buenos Aires Province, Argentina; family background not documented, but he joined the Argentine national volleyball team at age 15 in 1976.
current_position: Died on June 25, 2026, at age 65 after a battle with cancer; final role: head coach of the Argentina women's national volleyball team.

trajectory.event: Joined the Argentine national volleyball team, beginning a 12-year international playing career.
Won bronze at the FIVB World Championship as captain of Argentina's 'Generation of '82' on home soil.
Won bronze at the Pan American Games in Caracas.
Won Olympic bronze with Argentina at the Seoul Olympics.
Led Poland to the European Championship title as head coach, earning the Knight's Cross of Polonia Restituta.
Returned to coach the Argentina women's national team despite being diagnosed with cancer later that year.
Died on June 25, 2026, after a long battle with cancer.

name: Hiroshi Amano
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; was a PhD student at Nagoya University working on GaN-based blue LEDs. Key research publications came in the mid-1980s but the breakthrough recognition (Nobel Prize in Physics) came in 2014 at age 54.
early_history_summary: Amano joined Professor Isamu Akasaki's laboratory at Nagoya University in 1982 as an undergraduate, working on GaN-based blue LEDs. He received his bachelor's degree in 1983, master's in 1985, and doctoral degree in 1989, with his key breakthroughs coming in the late 1980s.
evidence_summary: Amano was a PhD student at Nagoya University at age 26, working under Professor Isamu Akasaki on GaN-based blue LEDs. While he published an important paper on GaN growth using an AlN buffer layer in 1986 at age 25, the recognition of this work as a milestone came decades later with the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2014. No independently verifiable material milestone was achieved by age 26.

name: José Nápoles
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; was a professional boxer building his record in Mexico after fleeing Cuba in 1962. Won the world welterweight title on April 18, 1969, at age 29, defeating Curtis Cokes.
early_history_summary: Nápoles debuted as a professional boxer on August 2, 1958, in Cuba at age 18, compiling over 30 victories before fleeing Castro's regime in 1962 and settling in Mexico City. He built an impressive record as a lightweight and junior welterweight contender but was unable to secure a title shot before moving up to welterweight in 1967.
family_context_summary: Born in Santiago de Cuba, Oriente, Cuba; fled Castro's Communist regime in 1962 and settled in Mexico City, becoming a Mexican citizen.
evidence_summary: Nápoles was a professional boxer who compiled an impressive record in Cuba and Mexico by age 26, but did not achieve a material milestone such as a world title by that age. He won the unified WBA/WBC welterweight championship at age 29 in 1969, and went on to become one of the greatest welterweights in boxing history, but fame and championship recognition arrived after age 26.

name: Reita Faria
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Miss World 1966 pageant in London at age 23, becoming the first Indian and first Asian to win the title, beating 51 delegates.
early_history_summary: Faria was born to Goan parents in Matunga, Bombay, and had a middle-class upbringing with her father working at a mineral water factory and mother owning a salon. She was a medical student at Grant Medical College when she entered the Miss Bombay contest on a lark, won it, then won Eve's Weekly Miss India, and went on to win Miss World 1966.
family_context_summary: Born to Goan parents in Matunga, Bombay; middle-class upbringing with father working at a mineral water factory and mother owning a salon in Marine Lines.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources, though her mother owned a salon which may have contributed to her grooming awareness.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Middle-class Goan family, mother owned salon, 5'8" height, medical student, Miss Bombay contest entry
evidence_summary: Faria was a middle-class medical student in Bombay who entered the Miss Bombay contest on a lark, with no prior pageant training or experience. Her natural physical attributes (5'8", statuesque by Indian standards) and poise carried her through Miss Bombay, Miss India, and ultimately Miss World 1966, where she became the first Indian and first Asian winner. She had minimal early advantages related to pageantry, entering the competition almost accidentally while pursuing a medical degree.
starting_point: Born to Goan parents in Matunga, Bombay; middle-class upbringing with father working at a mineral water factory and mother owning a salon in Marine Lines.
current_position: Retired physician living in Dublin, Ireland; former Miss World 1966 who declined modeling and acting careers to pursue medicine; grandmother of five.

trajectory.event: Won Miss World 1966 in London, becoming the first Indian and first Asian to win the title, beating 51 delegates.
Completed her one-year tenure as Miss World and declined lucrative modeling and acting contracts to focus on medical studies.
Married her mentor David Powell and continued medical studies at King's College Hospital, London.
Moved to Dublin, Ireland, and started her medical practice as a physician.
